title: Employer Benefit Charging — Schedule of Notice of Claim and Response Terms
content:
The terms below govern the notice of claim and the employer's separation and wage response under Employer Benefit Charging. They are set per charge class; every one of the seven classes carries the same figure for each term.

## Schedule

| Term | Separating Employer — Most Recent | Base Period Employer — Proportional Share | Continuing Part-Time Base Period Employer | Combined Wage Claim Contributing Employer | Extended Benefits State-Share Employer | Reimbursing Nonprofit Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar | Reimbursing Governmental Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Notice of claim mailed within (business days after the claim is filed) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Response window (calendar days after the notice of claim mailing date) | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| Response deadline extendable on request | No | No | No | No | No | No | No |
| Late response treated as timely when good cause is shown | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Third-party administrator with a power of attorney on file may respond and protest for the employer | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

Note to the term "Payments issued before a late response stay charged even if relief is later granted": for the relief credit of a protest decision and for the relief credit of a determination on a separation response, this term is applied only through the share by which a response received after the due date without good cause reduces that relief credit; no payment is kept charged on that account beyond it.

## Where notices go, how responses arrive, and which date counts

For every class:

- **Notice recipient.** Notices and statements are sent to the employer's address of record, or to its authorized agent.
- **Response channels.** A response is accepted through SIDES E-Response, the employer portal, fax or mail.
- **Response date.** The date that counts as the response date is the SIDES or employer-portal submission date, the fax receipt date, or the postmark date of a mailed response.

## Reading the schedule

- A ten-day response window means ten calendar days counted from the day after the notice of claim mailing date; weekends and holidays are not skipped because the unit is the calendar day.
- The notice of claim mailing term is counted in business days after the claim is filed, so it is a different unit from the response window.
- Because no class allows an extension, a request to extend the response deadline does not move it for any Employer Benefit Charging position.
